newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt, Dairy Board urge calm over diabetes link.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt, Dairy Board urge calm over diabetes link.

text.p: New Zealand's farm minister and vital dairy industry moved quickly to control damage on Thursday after researchers said milk could trigger diabetes in people genetically predisposed to the disease.
New Zealand is the world's largest dairy exporter, with exports worth NZ$5 billion annually.

Research by Professor Bob Elliott at Auckland Medical School linked the onset of insulin-dependent diabetes to milk containing a protein known as A1. About 80 percent of New Zealand's three-million-strong dairy herd have the gene that
Five percent of humans -- around 175,000 people in New Zealand -- are genetically vulnerable to insulin-dependent diabetes, but it develops in fewer than one percent of people.

"This is not the sort of thing that should cause any panic at all," Agriculture Minister Lockwood Smith said. "People have been drinking cow's milk, because it's a very healthy food, for years, for generations."
The New Zealand Dairy Board, which helped fund the research, said people should not avoid dairy products out of fear they might be predisposed to the disease.
Dairy Board public relations manager Neville Martin said sales could dip briefly on the back of the research but they should soon return to normal.
"Hopefully the public will finally be shown...both sides of the balanced picture, and realise there is absolutely no reason whatsoever to run around and say the sky is falling."
